item: streaming-speed: make streamed songs (YouTube Music, Spotify matched to YouTube) start faster on tap and on skip
currentBehaviour:
Read-only trace on main-6hltyd (= origin/main 86a5cce). A second reviewer re-checked every cited line. Android was compared on origin/android-int-oct3. All timings below are estimates from the code: nothing has been measured on a device, and the app has no stream-start instrumentation.

TAP -> FIRST AUDIO (stream not cached, process already warm). Every step below runs one after the other:
0. PlaybackStore.play (App/Stores/PlaybackStore.swift:62-76) -> DualDeckEngine.setQueue (App/Playback/DualDeckEngine.swift:116-130; it starts audio-session activation off-main at :123) -> loadCurrent (:351-382) throws both decks away and starts a Task -> DeckItemFactory.makeItem (App/Playback/Deck.swift:75-99).
1. URL resolver chain, outermost first (wired at App/AppEnvironment.swift:164 and :182-184):
   - SpotifyPlayableURLResolver (App/Services/Spotify/SpotifyYouTubeBridge.swift:103-118) looks up persistence.matchedVideoId (a hop onto the SwiftData actor).
   - If the song is unmatched, it runs TrackMatcher.findMatch on the spot (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/YouTube/TrackMatcher.swift:75-112): up to 3 song searches plus 1 video search, one after another, capped at 25 s (SpotifyYouTubeBridge.swift:81, :114).
   - Then InnerTubeSpotifyBridge (App/Services/Spotify/InnerTubeSpotifyBridge.swift:21-26) and StreamingPlayableURLResolver (App/Services/YouTube/YouTubePlayback.swift:12-17) check for a downloaded file, then a complete cache file, and otherwise return pixlstream://<id>. No network up to here for YouTube songs.
2. AVURLAsset plus loader (Deck.swift:81-82), then `await asset.loadTracks` (:83). AVFoundation's first loading request asks for content information AND bytes 0-1 (Apple forum thread 129155). It goes to YouTubeResourceLoader.serve (App/Services/YouTube/YouTubeResourceLoader.swift:61-92) -> StreamFetcher.info (App/Services/YouTube/StreamFetcher.swift:52-59). If the cache has no meta for the video, it calls fetch(0..<2) (:103-127), which first needs InnerTubeService.resolve (App/Services/YouTube/InnerTubeService.swift:56-65).
   a. The resolved-URL cache is in memory only (:23). On a miss, resolveFresh FIRST awaits remote.refreshIfNeeded() (:68): a GitHub raw fetch with a 10 s timeout (App/Services/YouTube/RemoteClientConfigStore.swift:32-43). The 6 h gate `lastAttempt` (:16, :34) is an in-memory var, so this blocking fetch runs on the first resolve of EVERY process launch (not only every 6 h), and every 6 h after that.
   b. ChainedYouTubeStreamResolver (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/YouTube/StreamResolution.swift:214-253) tries strategies strictly in order, each with a 15 s timeout (:179, :222). Order: VISIONOS, then IOS, then TVHTML5 / WEB / WEB_REMIX deciphered (pre-signed always come first: RemoteClientConfig.swift:145-154), then Piped (InnerTubeService.swift:73-84; up to 8 instances at 6 s each, tried one by one: Piped.swift:16-18 and :172-187).
      - Without a PoToken, IOS only offers muxed itag 18 (AudioFormatSelection.swift:58-63). That file carries video too, so it is several times larger.
   c. Each InnerTube attempt (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/YouTube/InnerTubeClient.swift:146-170) needs a visitorData first. That is one `visitor_id` POST per process (VisitorDataProvider :50-77, called at :157), done before the first player POST, and then the player POST itself. Spotify searches share the same provider (InnerTubeSpotifyBridge uses service.client), so it is paid once per process.
   d. Then applyNTransform (SignatureCipher.swift:283-287). It runs on pre-signed URLs too (StreamResolution.swift:75). Only when the URL carries `n` does it need ensurePlayerScript (:297-307 -> :319-324):
      - an iframe_api GET on every process;
      - base.js, cached on disk (App/Services/YouTube/YouTubeNetworking.swift:42-69), then regex extraction over ~2.5 MB with Array(js.utf16) copies (SignatureCipher.swift:98, :109);
      - a brand-new JSContext for every evaluate (App/Services/YouTube/JavaScriptCoreEvaluator.swift:15-25).
      A failed download is not cached (`cached = script` stores nil at :305), so while youtube.com fails, every URL repeats iframe_api + base.js.
      Whether VISIONOS URLs carry `n` is UNKNOWN. The code comments assume they don't (InnerTubeService.swift:7; SpotifyYouTubeBridge.swift:33-34). yt-dlp's VISIONOS entry has REQUIRE_JS_PLAYER False (_base.py:296-310), but that only means yt-dlp doesn't fetch the player before the player request: it still solves `n` for any format URL that has one (_video.py ~3573-3580). The attempt detail can't tell either, because 'n sin cambiar' (StreamResolution.swift:76) means both 'no n' and 'transform failed'.
   e. A 2-byte googlevideo GET (StreamFetcher.swift:114, `session.data(for:)`) to the per-video rrN---sn-… host. It pays the new TCP+TLS connection plus a round trip and carries only the 2 bytes AVFoundation asked for. The format's contentLength is parsed (InnerTubeParsing.swift:64) but dropped: ResolvedStream (InnerTubeModels.swift:88-98) has only url / UA / strategy.
3. AVFoundation's next data request (to end of resource, per thread 129155; AVPlayer may cancel it and re-issue ranged requests) -> StreamFetcher.data (:65-73):
   - The cache holds bytes 0-1, so the first answer is those 2 bytes from disk (:68-69). Then it fetches a 1 MiB chunk (chunkSize at :43) with `session.data(for:)`. Nothing more reaches AVPlayer until the whole MiB has arrived (about 0.8 s at 10 Mbps, about 2.7 s at 3 Mbps).
   - If AVPlayer cancels a loading request mid-chunk, the loader's task is cancelled (YouTubeResourceLoader.swift:47-53) and the partial download is thrown away, because nothing is stored until the body completes (:114-118).
   - The chunks then go one after another, with no pipelining.
   - Each chunk rewrites the JSON meta atomically (StreamCache.swift:98-113, :177-180).
4. Then `load(.duration)` runs after the track load (Deck.swift:88). It is probably near-instant once the moov box has been parsed. Then the AVPlayerItem and processing-tap mix are built (:93-96), and install / Deck.load / startActive -> playImmediately(atRate:) (Deck.swift:210-213). automaticallyWaitsToMinimizeStalling is true (:138) and preferredForwardBufferDuration is the default.
Failure handling (StreamFetcher.swift:119-123):
- 401/403/404/410 immediately invalidates the URL and excludes that strategy, up to maxResolutions = 3 (:44, :105). Android oct3 first refreshes the same client, because the cause may just be an IP change (CloudStreamProxy.kt:260-279, MAX_UPSTREAM_ATTEMPTS = 4 at :93).
- 429/5xx throws straight away -> the loader fails the request -> loadTracks throws -> DualDeckEngine.loadFailed (:396-408) skips to the next song while playing. formatChanged (StreamFetcher.swift:152-157) ends the same way: a skip, not a reload.

PREFETCH (YouTubePlayback.swift:42-90):
- On every track or queue change it resolves the next song's URL (:79).
- It fetches that song's first 1 MiB only 30 s before the current song ends (:49, :82-87).
- It finds the next song with YouTubeSongIdentity.videoId(for:) (InnerTubeService.swift:159-169), which returns nil for Spotify songs, because their contentUri is spotify://<id> (App/Services/Spotify/SpotifyUnifiedLibrary.swift:78). So the prefetcher never pre-matches, pre-resolves or prefetches Spotify songs.
- Exception: with crossfade ON (default off, SettingsStore.swift:369), a crossfade plan builds the next item through the full resolver 1.5 s into the song (CrossfadeScheduler.debounceMs = 1500; DualDeckEngine+Crossfade.swift:105-109 -> prepareIncoming :130-151). That does match, resolve and load Spotify songs early, and parks a paused AVPlayerItem on the idle deck.
- Android oct3 warms the next Spotify track (match + URL only, no bytes) 1.5 s after playback starts, only while playing, re-checked every 60 s (origin/android-int-oct3 MusicService.kt:1272-1297, StreamUrlPrefetcher.kt, StreamUrlCache.kt).

SKIP (DualDeckEngine.swift:435-446):
- jump only reuses active.upcoming, but Deck.append (Deck.swift:176-183) is never called, so that list is always empty.
- advance -> loadCurrent -> cancelCrossfadePlan (DualDeckEngine+Crossfade.swift:310-324) throws away preparedIncoming even when it is exactly the target.
- So every skip is a full makeItem: InnerTube (unless the URL was pre-resolved), the 2-byte request and 1 MiB from the network (unless the 30-s prefetch already ran).
- The gapless hand-over (crossfade off, the default) prepares only 4.5 s before the transition point (Crossfade.swift:49-51, :112). For a Spotify song that is not yet matched, that means match + resolve + first request + 1 MiB inside 4.5 s, or there is a gap. Crossfade plans prepare right after the 1.5 s debounce.

ALREADY GOOD:
- Replaying a recently played song: cache meta and head bytes are on disk, so content info and the first bytes need no network and no InnerTube call at all (StreamFetcher.swift:53-55, :68-69). Resolve happens only when playback reaches uncached bytes, and by then cached audio is already playing.
- In-flight resolutions are coalesced (InnerTubeService.swift:59-63).
- base.js is cached on disk.
- Audio-session activation is prepared off-main.
- Complete or downloaded songs play from local files.
- The restored queue's current song is loaded at launch (DualDeckEngine.swift:320-338).

ANDROID (oct3) features iOS lacks (origin/android-int-oct3:data/stream/CloudStreamProxy.kt):
- It streams the upstream body to the player in 64 KB writes (:360-366) instead of waiting for whole chunks.
- It takes the size from Content-Range, with `clen` only as a fallback (:216-219). It needs no separate probe because the proxy forwards ExoPlayer's own range request; AVFoundation, by contrast, always asks for content info + 2 bytes first.
- It uses 512 KB chunks (:92).
- It retries 401/403/404/410/429/5xx up to 4 attempts. It refreshes the same client first, and backs off 250 ms × attempt for 429/5xx (:253-279).
rootCause:
Not a bug: it's latency built into the design. Ranked by likely size (unmeasured):
1. The first network round trip carries only the 2 bytes AVFoundation asks for. The next one must download a whole 1 MiB before AVPlayer gets any audio (StreamFetcher.swift:43, :56, :66-72, :114).
2. Upcoming songs get no head bytes until 30 s before the end. While crossfade is off (the default), Spotify songs are never pre-matched, pre-resolved or prefetched (YouTubePlayback.swift:49, :66-67). So skips, and Spotify auto-advances, run the whole network path one step after another.
3. The first resolve of every cold launch pays two things:
   - a blocking GitHub remote-config fetch (InnerTubeService.swift:68; the in-memory gate is at RemoteClientConfigStore.swift:16, :34);
   - the visitor_id POST (InnerTubeClient.swift:50-77, :157).
   If VISIONOS URLs carry `n` (unverified), it also pays iframe_api + the base.js regex + a JSContext (SignatureCipher.swift:283-324).
4. Clients are tried strictly one at a time with a 15 s timeout each (StreamResolution.swift:179, :218-249).
5. Skips never reuse a prepared item (DualDeckEngine.swift:438; Crossfade.swift:317-323).
alternativeCauses: If the slow starts are mostly Spotify songs, the main cost may be on-demand matching. TrackMatcher runs up to 4 searches one after another (TrackMatcher.swift:100-106), with a 25 s cap (SpotifyYouTubeBridge.swift:81). Check how many tracks are still PENDING or UNMATCHED in the Spotify dashboard.

If VISIONOS is failing for Hoa's IP (bot check), every song pays for a failed VISIONOS player call before the IOS fallback. IOS without a PoToken only gives muxed itag 18, which is several times larger, so the first MiB holds far less audio. The deep probe's 'Last resolution' lines in PlaybackDiagnosticsView (App/Features/YouTube/PlaybackDiagnosticsView.swift:51-52) would show this.

VISIONOS URLs may carry `n`. In that case every cold launch's first resolve also pays the iframe_api GET, the base.js read and regex, and JSContext work inside the VISIONOS attempt (SignatureCipher.swift:283-324). R9 then moves up the list. The current diagnostics can't tell, because 'n sin cambiar' covers both 'no n' and 'failed'.
Throughput limits rather than latency, for example cellular Low Data Mode or a throttled googlevideo URL. If the URL carries `n` and the transform silently fails, googlevideo throttles the download.

AVPlayer may cancel its optimistic 'to end' request and re-plan (thread 129155 describes exactly this). Each cancel throws away an in-flight 1 MiB chunk (YouTubeResourceLoader.swift:47-53; nothing is stored before the body completes, StreamFetcher.swift:114-118). R12 should log loader-request arrivals and cancellations.

Main-actor congestion during the full-player expand animation could delay the loadCurrent Task, the install and the KVO hops (Deck.swift:139-144). That would show as a gap between the network finishing and playImmediately.

The SwiftData PersistenceActor may be busy with SpotifyMatchRunner batch writes (Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlNet/Spotify/SpotifyMatchRunner.swift:81-92), delaying the matchedVideoId lookup at tap time.
research:
These are the findings that change the plan. Each was checked against the source this time; URLs are in the sources list below.
- AVFoundation's first loader request carries a contentInformationRequest AND a dataRequest for bytes 0-1. The next request is an optimistic 'to end of resource' request, which AVPlayer may cancel and replace with ranged requests (forum thread 129155). The previously cited thread 735572 does NOT say this.
  - So the first network round trip can't be skipped: the 2 bytes must be delivered.
  - Answering the content info from the URL's `clen` (old R1) saves nothing unless a request ever arrives without a dataRequest.
  - The lever is making that unavoidable first round trip fetch a useful amount (R2).
- dataRequest docs: 'The value of this property is nil if no data is being requested'. 'If the loading request's contentInformationRequest isn't nil, set that request's properties before you respond to any data request.'
- respond(with:) (iOS 7): 'may be invoked multiple times on the same instance … to provide the full range of requested data incrementally.'
- automaticallyWaitsToMinimizeStalling and playImmediately(atRate:): playImmediately already plays whatever is buffered. So AVPlayer settings are not the lever; how fast the first bytes arrive is.
- preferredForwardBufferDuration: 0 lets the system choose. It does not affect start-up.
- AVURLAssetPreferPreciseDurationAndTimingKey: the default (false) is right for playback.
- isEntireLengthAvailableOnDemand (iOS 16): set it only when all data is cached or local.
- URLRequest.assumesHTTP3Capable (iOS 14.5): 'Enables QUIC racing without HTTP/3 service discovery.'
  - WWDC21 10094 (Accelerate networking with HTTP/3 and QUIC) and 10239 (Reduce network delays for your app) say fewer round trips is the main lever: TLS 1.3 over TCP needs 2 round trips before the request, QUIC 1.
  - Google's Cloud CDN post says HTTP/3 'reduced video rebuffer times on YouTube by 9%'.
- URLRequest.allowsConstrainedNetworkAccess (iOS 13): 'Limit your app's use of constrained network access to user-initiated tasks, and put off discretionary tasks', which fits speculative prefetch.
- URLSessionTask.delegate (iOS 15), URLSession.bytes(for:delegate:) (iOS 15) and URLSessionDataDelegate are the options for streaming response bodies (R10).
- yt-dlp:
  - VISIONOS has REQUIRE_JS_PLAYER False (_base.py:296-310). Its client-loop code (_video.py:3069-3075) shows this only skips fetching the player up front. Format URLs with an `n` query still go through solve_js_challenges, or the format is dropped (_video.py ~3573-3580). So 'VISIONOS needs no base.js' is unproven: measure it.
  - yt-dlp downloads YouTube https formats in CHUNK_SIZE = 10 << 20 ranges (_video.py:3229, :3613). Chunks of 128 KiB to 2 MiB are well inside that.
- 'The Tail at Scale': send a hedged request only after the first has been outstanding past ~p95 latency.
- Android oct3's CloudStreamProxy (:92, :216-219, :253-279, :360-366), StreamUrlPrefetcher/StreamUrlCache and MusicService.updateNextStreamPrefetch (:1272-1297; prepares only while player.isPlaying) are the reference behaviours.
- Ledger check (docs/api-notes.md):
  - OSSignposter(subsystem:category:)/beginInterval/endInterval (row :463) and Synchronization.Mutex (rows :91, :229) are already recorded.
  - NSLock is allowed only in synchronous helpers (:115). Prefer Mutex for the new timings store.
  - JSContext.objectForKeyedSubscript(_:)'s doc page lists iOS 16.0 (not 7.0).
- Build settings: project.yml:20 sets SWIFT_APPROACHABLE_CONCURRENCY = YES, so nonisolated async code runs on the caller's actor. Work started from the @MainActor prefetcher runs on main between awaits unless detached or @concurrent (pattern already used at App/Services/ML/AudioPCMReader.swift:18).

options.name: R1 (rejected as a speed-up). Learn the size from the URL's `clen` instead of probing
options.description: The old plan said this saves one googlevideo round trip. It doesn't. AVFoundation's first loader request asks for content info AND bytes 0-1 (thread 129155), and those 2 bytes still need a network GET. Today the probe GET's bytes serve that dataRequest from cache (StreamFetcher.swift:56 then :68-69). With R1 the same GET just moves into data(). R2 instead makes that unavoidable first GET fetch 128 KiB and read the size from Content-Range. Android uses `clen` only as a fallback when Content-Range is missing (CloudStreamProxy.kt:216-219). Revisit only if the R12 log shows a content-info request with dataRequest == nil.
options.cons: None; it was a misread of AVFoundation's request pattern.

options.name: R2. Make the first round trip useful: small first chunk, growing after
options.description: The content-info request's fetch downloads 0..<128 KiB instead of 0..<2. The size still comes from Content-Range, the same as today. The 2 bytes for that request, and the first 128 KiB of the following 'to end' request, are then served from disk. Later network fetches per loading request ramp 128 KiB -> 512 KiB -> 2 MiB (capped at 2 MiB, far under yt-dlp's 10 MiB chunks). A smaller in-flight chunk also loses less when AVPlayer cancels a request. Saves about 0.15 s on fast Wi-Fi, 0.7 s at 10 Mbps and 2+ s at 3 Mbps (it replaces a 1 MiB wait with a 128 KiB one). Risk: low. Effort: S-M.
options.pros: Most of the gain of true streaming with almost no new machinery; it keeps session.data(for:).
options.cons: 3-4 extra small requests per song. Concurrent loading requests can still fetch the same bytes twice.

options.name: R3. Prefetcher v2: Spotify included, head bytes early
options.description: The YouTubePrefetcher maps the next song through the engine's full resolver. So Spotify songs are matched (on demand if needed), resolved and prefetched like YouTube songs. It downloads the first 512 KiB of the next song (and the one after it if Hoa wants) about 3 s into playback, only while playing (Android's gate), honouring Low Data Mode. The existing top-up to 1 MiB 30 s before the end stays. A next song whose meta and head bytes are cached starts with no network at all. Saves 1-3 s per manual skip (to about 0.2-0.3 s) and stops gaps on Spotify auto-advance. Risk: low-medium (data use). Effort: M.
options.pros: The biggest win for skips. It brings back Android oct3's next-track preparation, and goes beyond it (head bytes).
options.cons: About 0.5 MB of cellular data per upcoming song, even if it's never played. On-demand matching now runs in the background (more YouTube search calls).

options.name: R4. Don't block on the remote client table
options.description: InnerTubeService.resolveFresh stops awaiting remote.refreshIfNeeded(): the refresh runs in the background at utility priority, and resolution uses the current table. Also seed the in-memory gate from the saved remote-config.json modification date, so relaunches within 6 h of a good fetch skip the network entirely. Saves one GitHub round trip (~0.1-0.5 s) on the first stream of EVERY cold launch, and up to 10 s on a flaky network. Risk: very low. Effort: S.
options.pros: Trivial change; it affects every cold launch, not just every 6 h as previously thought.
options.cons: A freshly fixed table takes effect one resolution later.

options.name: R5a. Retry like Android (reliability)
options.description: On a 401/403/404/410: invalidate and re-resolve once with the same strategies before excluding one, because the IP may have changed. Retry 429/500/502/503/504 after sleeping 250 ms × attempt. Raise maxResolutions from 3 to 4 (Android MAX_UPSTREAM_ATTEMPTS). The formatChanged check stays. Mostly fewer skipped songs rather than faster starts. Risk: low. Effort: S.
options.pros: Parity with Android oct3's retry rules (CloudStreamProxy.kt:253-279).
options.cons: A genuinely blocked client costs one extra round trip before the fallback.

options.name: R5b (optional, low value). Persist resolved URLs across launches
options.description:
Save the resolved url, user agent, strategy and expiry so a new process skips InnerTube. Value is small:
- replays with cached head bytes already start without any resolve;
- songs never played before were never resolved.
It only helps the first uncached fetch of a song resolved in an earlier process within ~6 h. If done, keep it inside InnerTubeService: a small JSON in Caches/YouTube/resolved, with an app-side Codable mirror because PixlNet's ResolvedStream is not Codable. Don't put it in StreamCache.Meta: that couples URLs to byte eviction and would need the service/cache init reorder. Risk: medium-low (IP-bound URLs). Effort: S-M.
options.pros: Removes a few InnerTube calls after relaunch.
options.cons: Stores IP-bound URLs on disk; a stale one costs a 403 round trip after a Wi-Fi/cellular switch.

options.name: R6. HTTP/3 to googlevideo
options.description: Set URLRequest.assumesHTTP3Capable = true on range requests whose host ends with `.googlevideo.com` (not on Piped hosts). Saves about 1 round trip (~50-100 ms on LTE) per song, because each song usually lives on a new rrN---sn-… host. Risk: very low (it falls back to TCP). Effort: S.
options.pros: One line, Apple-documented, and QUIC connection migration helps across Wi-Fi/cellular switches.
options.cons: No gain where UDP is blocked. Needs an API-ledger entry.

options.name: R7. Skip into the already-prepared next song
options.description: jump(to:) takes over preparedIncoming when it is exactly the target song, instead of cancelCrossfadePlan throwing it away. Coverage: with crossfade on, the item exists from ~1.5 s into the song, so nearly every skip; with gapless (the default), only the last ~4.5 s. Saves the whole makeItem (50 ms to several seconds) in those windows. Risk: medium (deck state machine). Effort: M.
options.pros: Instant skips in that window; uses machinery that already exists.
options.cons: Touches the engine's state machine; needs a DualDeckEngineTests case.

options.name: R8. Overlap YouTube clients after a delay
options.description: ChainedYouTubeStreamResolver gets an opt-in hedge delay: start the next strategy if the current one hasn't answered within ~1.5 s, or as soon as it fails; first success wins. The per-strategy timeout drops from 15 s to ~8 s on iOS. Android's default behaviour stays for its parity tests. Saves 0 on typical starts and up to 13 s when VISIONOS is slow or hung. Do it only if R12 shows slow or failing VISIONOS. Risk: medium (extra YouTube requests could look bot-like). Effort: M.
options.cons: Diverges from Android; needs new PixlNet tests. Concurrent strategies share InnerTubeClient.lastFailureReason, so a losing attempt's detail can show another client's error (diagnostics only).

options.name: R9. Cipher and JavaScriptCore warm-up (conditional on R12)
options.pros: Removes the 2.5 MB regex work from cold starts.
options.cons: Needs PlayerScript Codable and a small PixlNet protocol addition; possibly off the main path.

options.name: R10. Real streaming responses (later)
options.pros: The best long-term design, and it removes duplicate downloads.
options.cons: The biggest refactor (StreamFetcher, StreamCache, YouTubeResourceLoader). Do it only if measurement after R2 still shows a gap to the first byte.

options.name: R11. Faster on-demand Spotify matching
options.description: On the play-time path only: after the first query misses, run the remaining song queries and the video search in parallel, then judge them in the original order (same result as Android's matcher). Saves 0.3-2 s for unmatched tracks played on the spot. Risk: low-medium (more search requests). Effort: S-M.

options.name: R12. Measure first
options.pros: Hoa can see the gains on the phone without a Mac or Instruments. It settles the open questions (VISIONOS `n`, cancellations, VISIONOS failures) that decide R8/R9/R10.

options.name: Rejected: local HTTP proxy (Android-style), HLS, download-then-play, PoToken/WKWebView warm-up, a 'warm asset' cache
options.description:
- The resource loader already does the proxy's job without a server.
- YouTube's HLS manifests come only from the IOS client with a PoToken, are muxed and need more round trips.
- Download-then-play starts slower.
- PoTokens are only for the signed-in WEB_REMIX fallback, and warming a WKWebView is heavy (AGENTS: nothing heavy at launch).
- A loaded AVURLAsset kept for the next song may keep issuing 'to end' requests and download the whole song.

recommendedPlan.change:
R12, measure first.
- Add `nonisolated final class PlaybackStartTimings: Sendable` with a `static let shared`. State lives in a `Synchronization.Mutex` (ledger rows :91/:229; unlike NSLock it is safe to call from async code).
- Key everything by the item URL string, so App/Playback stays free of YouTube code. The YouTube layer builds the key with YouTubeSongIdentity.streamURL(videoId:).
- Record these marks:
  - makeItem start, URL resolved, loadTracks done, item built (DeckItemFactory);
  - first `.playing` for the active item (DualDeckEngine.handle `.statusChanged`, after the `deck === active` guard);
  - resolve start/end with strategy, remote-config wait and `hasN = URLCoding.androidQueryParameter(url, "n") != nil` (InnerTubeService.resolveFresh);
  - each loader request's arrival, offset, length, toEnd, content-info flag and cancellation (YouTubeResourceLoader);
  - first network body and first respond(with:) (StreamFetcher / serve).

R4.
- Add `func refreshInBackground() { Task(priority: .utility) { await self.refreshIfNeeded() } }` to the actor. The existing `lastAttempt` assignment before the await (:35) already stops duplicate fetches.
- In resolveFresh, replace `await remote.refreshIfNeeded()` with `await remote.refreshInBackground()`, which returns at once. Resolution keeps using `remote.current()` through the `strategies:` closure (:49).
- In refreshIfNeeded, when `lastAttempt == nil`, seed it from the remote-config.json file's contentModificationDate. URLResourceValues is already used at YouTubeNetworking.swift:83-86, so no new API. A relaunch within 6 h of a successful fetch then makes no request. Only successful fetches write the file (:41-42).

R2.
- Add `static let startFetchBytes: Int64 = 128 << 10` and `maxFetchBytes: Int64 = 2 << 20` (both far below yt-dlp's 10 MiB). Keep chunkSize only if something else references it.
- fetch gains `readAhead: Int64 = 0`. The Range header covers `range.lowerBound ..< min(max(range.upperBound, range.lowerBound + readAhead), nextCachedStart ?? .max, meta?.contentLength ?? .max)`, while store() keeps returning only `range` (:161-165) and caching the whole body. A range past EOF is clamped by the server (206 with the real Content-Range).
- info(): when there is no meta, call `fetch(videoId:, range: 0..<2, readAhead: startFetchBytes)`. The content-info request's 2 bytes and the next 'to end' request's first 128 KiB then come from disk.
- data(videoId:from:upTo:fetchSize:) fetches up to `min(offset + fetchSize, end, nextCachedStart)` and returns all of it.
- serve's loop starts fetchSize at startFetchBytes for its first network fetch and multiplies by 4 per network iteration, up to maxFetchBytes. Cache hits don't advance the ramp.
- prefetch() and fillCache() pass maxFetchBytes.
- Test with a URLProtocol stub session in AppTests/YouTubeServicesTests.swift: assert the first GET's Range is bytes=0-131071 and that the next request is served from the cache.

R3, rewrite the prefetcher.
- Resolver: no new closure is needed. The prefetcher already holds `engine` (@MainActor) and reads `engine.factory.resolver` when it plans. That happens after AppEnvironment.swift:182-184 has installed the Spotify resolver.
- Candidates: the entry at queue.nextIndexForAutoAdvance (plus nextIndexForSkip if it differs; plus +1 if Hoa picks depth 2). Keep only songs where `YouTubeSongIdentity.videoId(for:) != nil || SpotifyPlayableURLResolver.spotifyId(of:) != nil`, and skip downloaded files.
- Gate everything on `engine.playWhenReady`, like Android (MusicService.kt:1274, :1287). That also keeps it quiet during Spotify Connect sessions, where PlaybackStore.play passes playWhenReady false (PlaybackStore.swift:67-71).
- Phase A, after 1.5 s: `url = await resolver.playableURL(for: song)`, which pre-matches Spotify songs; then `videoId = YouTubeSongIdentity.videoId(from: url)` (a file URL means nothing to do); then `await service.resolve(videoId:)`.
- Phase B, once position ≥ 3 s: `await fetcher.prefetch(videoId:, bytes: 512 << 10, allowsConstrained: false)`.
- Phase C: the existing top-up to 1 MiB at 30 s before the end.
- Off-main: approachable concurrency (project.yml:20) runs nonisolated async code on the caller's actor. Capture the Sendable resolver, service and fetcher, and run Phases A/B in `Task.detached(priority: .utility)`, or mark StreamFetcher.prefetch `@concurrent` like AudioPCMReader.swift:18. Read positions on the main actor.
- Play/pause:
  - PlaybackServices already owns the single `engine.onPlayingChanged` closure (:117-123). Add `var onPlayStateChanged: ((Bool) -> Void)?` to PlaybackServices and call it inside that closure.
  - YouTubeServices.install wires it to a new `prefetcher.playingChanged(_:)`. Don't reuse upcomingChanged(): its early return at YouTubePlayback.swift:74 makes it a no-op.
  - Pause cancels Phases A/B; resume re-plans.
- Keep a single task, as today.

recommendedPlan.change:
R10: a delegate-based ranged download on a dedicated URLSession.
- urlSession(_:dataTask:didReceive:completionHandler:) validates status, Content-Range and type.
- urlSession(_:dataTask:didReceive:) writes each slice to StreamCache and wakes waiters.
- Add a per-video in-flight registry, so a loading request whose offset lies inside an active download waits for it instead of opening a new request.
- The loader answers in ≥ 64 KiB slices.

risks: Format checks: a Content-Range total that differs from the cached meta, or a re-resolved URL with another itag, makes store() throw formatChanged (StreamFetcher.swift:152-157). The loader then fails the request and DualDeckEngine.loadFailed skips to the next song (:396-408); the item is NOT reloaded, contrary to the old R1 risk note. Any new code that seeds meta early, or re-resolves after bytes were cached, must keep this in mind.
Smaller first chunks (R2) mean 3-4 extra requests per song. That stays far below yt-dlp's 10 MiB chunking, but watch for 429s: the R5a retry rules handle them.

Approachable concurrency (project.yml:20): nonisolated async helpers called from @MainActor code run on the main actor between awaits. Without Task.detached or @concurrent, prefetch Data copies and TrackMatcher scoring would land on main during playback.

The R5a re-resolve must not exclude the strategy on the first 403. Otherwise the fallback to IOS can switch to muxed itag 18, and a song with cached bytes fails with formatChanged, which means a skip.

Overlapping YouTube clients (R8) sends extra player requests, which could raise YouTube's bot scoring for Hoa's IP. Keep the delay around the 95th-percentile VISIONOS latency (≥ 1.5 s) and keep Android's sequential mode as the default in PixlNet. The shared lastFailureReason makes losing attempts' details unreliable.

Reusing the prepared item (R7) touches the deck state machine (hand-over, fade, tap ramps).
- Forgetting to clear the incoming crossfade ramp would play silence.
- Calling deck methods through the computed `idle` after the swap hits the wrong deck.
- It needs DualDeckEngineTests cases and a check on Hoa's phone.

A 'warm asset' cache (keeping a loaded AVURLAsset for the next song) is deliberately left out: it may keep issuing 'to end' loader requests and download the whole next song. Note that crossfade-on already parks a paused AVPlayerItem for the next song (Crossfade.swift:149).
Nothing compiles locally. Every App/ change is verified only on CI (xcode-27). The PixlCore changes must also build and test on Windows Swift.

The latency estimates are code-derived, and two key facts are unknown: whether VISIONOS URLs carry `n`, and how often AVPlayer cancels its first 'to end' request. Ship R12 in the first batch so R8, R9 and R10 can be decided from Hoa's phone.
ownerDecisions: How many upcoming songs should be prepared ahead, and on which networks? Suggested: next 1 song on cellular and next 2 on Wi-Fi, 512 KB each, none in Low Data Mode, only while music is playing.
May the app quietly pre-match Spotify songs that are next in the queue (more background YouTube searches while music plays)? Suggested: yes, only for the next 1-2 queue entries.

When the first YouTube client is slow, may the app ask a second client at the same time after about 1.5 s? That gives faster worst cases but slightly more requests to YouTube. Suggested: decide after the new diagnostics line shows how often VISIONOS is slow; Android unchanged.

These speed-ups make iOS behave differently from Android in a few places (bigger first fetch, head-byte prefetch, overlapping clients, parallel Spotify matching). OK to diverge here, or should the same changes be ported to Android too? Suggested: iOS first, list them in parity.md for Android later.

Optional and low value: may PixlAudio remember YouTube stream links on the phone between launches (they expire within about 6 hours)? It only speeds up the first uncached part of a song resolved before the relaunch. Suggested: not now.

If YouTube's VISIONOS client fails, iOS falls back to the IOS client, which only gives a larger video+audio file (slower to start, more data). The TV client (audio-only, but it needs the cipher) can come before IOS only by dropping IOS from remote/config.json `preSignedOrder`, because pre-signed clients always run first (RemoteClientConfig.swift:145-154). Suggested: decide after measuring with the new diagnostics line.
